extension.description: Reviews rls-saboteur runs. It reads the source database read-only, creates temporary labelled copies of it on the same server, breaks policies only in those copies, and drops them. Also reviews the flags that let it run against a non-local database, terminate other sessions on the source, or leave outbound HTTP on in the copies. Direct runs with --help, -h, --version, -v, --dry-run or --checks-only are not matched (launcher forms stay in review). Covers the rls-saboteur executable and npx, bunx, pnpx, pnpm, yarn, npm exec, npm x, bun x, pnpm dlx and yarn dlx launches, including versioned launches (rls-saboteur@tag).
extension.name: rls-saboteur command protection

permissions.description: Identifies rls-saboteur runs that create and drop temporary labelled database copies on the target server and run a test command against them.
permissions.label: rls-saboteur database copy run
safer_guidance: Point rls-saboteur at a local or disposable database, never production.
Read the plan it prints before answering yes; pass --yes only for a run whose plan you have read.
Run `rls-saboteur --dry-run` or `--checks-only` first; both read the catalogue and run no tests.

permissions.description: Identifies rls-saboteur runs that disable its refusal to run against a database that is not local.
permissions.label: rls-saboteur remote database override
safer_guidance: Do not pass --allow-remote-i-understand-this-locks-tables against a production or shared database.
Point --db-url at a local or disposable database; copying a live database locks it for the length of the copy and can stall it.

permissions.description: Identifies rls-saboteur runs that approve terminating the other sessions connected to the source database for a moment, to take the first copy.
permissions.label: rls-saboteur close other sessions
safer_guidance: Do not pass --close-sessions to a database that other people or services are using; stop them yourself, or use a disposable database.
Without --close-sessions the tool asks you first, or exits 2 and names the flag when there is no terminal; nothing is closed.

permissions.description: Identifies rls-saboteur runs that leave outbound HTTP switched on inside the temporary copies.
permissions.label: rls-saboteur outbound network left on
safer_guidance: Leave outbound HTTP switched off (the default) unless a test needs a call out, and then use a database that holds no real personal data.
Copies hold a full copy of the source data; --no-isolate-network lets triggers and functions in a copy send it to outside services.

rules.description: Identifies rls-saboteur runs. It reads the source database read-only, creates temporary labelled copies of it on the same server with CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE, breaks policies only inside those copies, runs the test command against a copy, and drops the copies it made. It never changes the source database. It asks for approval of a plan before it starts (--yes approves the plan when there is no terminal), refuses non-local hosts unless --allow-remote-i-understand-this-locks-tables is passed, and refuses a source over 2GB unless --max-size is passed. The role (or --admin-url) must be able to create and drop databases. Direct runs with --help, -h, --version, -v, --dry-run or --checks-only stay unmatched; launcher forms of those stay in review.
safer_alternatives: Point rls-saboteur at a local or disposable database, never production.
Read the plan it prints before answering yes; pass --yes only for a run whose plan you have read.
Run `rls-saboteur --dry-run` or `--checks-only` first; both read the catalogue and run no tests.
rules.title: rls-saboteur database copy run

rules.description: Identifies rls-saboteur with --allow-remote-i-understand-this-locks-tables, the flag that turns off its refusal to run against a database that is not local (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1 and the Docker host). Copying a live database locks it for the length of the copy and can stall it.
safer_alternatives: Do not pass --allow-remote-i-understand-this-locks-tables against a production or shared database.
Point --db-url at a local or disposable database; copying a live database locks it for the length of the copy and can stall it.
rules.title: rls-saboteur remote database override

rules.description: Identifies rls-saboteur with --close-sessions, which approves terminating the other sessions connected to the source database on the same server for a moment, to take the first copy. Applications on those connections lose them and must reconnect. It works only on a local source, and --yes does not give this approval. Direct runs with --help, -h, --version, -v, --dry-run or --checks-only stay unmatched.
safer_alternatives: Do not pass --close-sessions to a database that other people or services are using; stop them yourself, or use a disposable database.
Without --close-sessions the tool asks you first, or exits 2 and names the flag when there is no terminal; nothing is closed.
rules.title: rls-saboteur close other sessions

rules.description: Identifies rls-saboteur with --no-isolate-network, which leaves outbound HTTP switched on inside the temporary copies (by default the net, pg_net and http functions do nothing in a copy). Triggers and functions in a copy can then call outside services with the copied data. Direct runs with --help, -h, --version, -v, --dry-run or --checks-only stay unmatched.
safer_alternatives: Leave outbound HTTP switched off (the default) unless a test needs a call out, and then use a database that holds no real personal data.
Copies hold a full copy of the source data; --no-isolate-network lets triggers and functions in a copy send it to outside services.
rules.title: rls-saboteur outbound network left on

safer_alternatives: Point rls-saboteur at a local or disposable database, never production.
Run `rls-saboteur --dry-run` or `--checks-only` first; both read the catalogue and run no tests.
